title: refactor(ci): modernize pipelines - split lint/test/release workflows, bump actions & deps
author: Evelyn Chen
description: Motivation: CI runtime has grown noisy and slow as we accumulated monolithic workflows. This PR refactors our GitHub Actions pipelines to improve parallelism, cache hygiene, and observability. Goals: 1) Split monorepo workflows into focused lint, test, and release pipelines to reduce runtime and make failures easier to triage. 2) Upgrade GH Actions and key actions (actions/checkout, actions/cache, actions/setup-node) to latest major versions and bump the default Node runtime to 20 where safe. 3) Improve cache keys and add restore/fallback layers for flaky integration tests. 4) Reduce false positives by running lint in a more deterministic container and adding explicit step-level timeouts. Checklist: - [x] Split .github/workflows/main.yml into lint.yml, test.yml, release.yml - [x] Bump actions/checkout@v3 -> @v4, actions/cache@v2 -> @v4, actions/setup-node@v3 -> @v4 - [x] Introduce build matrix that runs unit tests and integration tests in parallel with tighter resource constraints - [x] Add cache warmup script and TTL-based pruning (scripts/ci/cache-setup.sh) - [x] Update developer docs: README_CI.md and tools/gh-actions/upgrade.md Related: ENG-9876 (CI perf), ENG-10234 (release automation hygiene). Risk profile: low; no runtime code changes. Release notes: repo CI improvements and workflow refactor to speed up PR validation and reduce flakiness. For rollout, workflows are gated behind a short beta window (branch filter: refactor/ci/* and ci-rollout tag) before enabling org-wide. If a step regresses, revert using the revert action documented in README_CI.md.
commits: feat(ci): split monorepo workflow into lint.yml, test.yml, release.yml
chore(ci): add cache-setup script and improve cache keys
docs(ci): add README_CI.md and upgrade guidance
fix(ci): tighten timeouts and add step-level retry for flaky network calls

review_comments: Aisha Kapoor: Nice separation — can we add an explicit matrix axis for 'fast' vs 'slow' integration tests so we don't block PRs for long-running suites?
Evelyn Chen: Good idea. Added 'suite: fast, slow' axis and a 'fast-only' label to gate long runs. See test.yml (matrix.suite).
Benji Park: Please confirm we won't regress cached artifacts across self-hosted runners. Suggest adding TTL and explicit cache pruning steps.
Evelyn Chen: Added scripts/ci/cache-setup.sh and infra/ci/cache-config.yaml with TTL=7d and a prune step that runs weekly on the self-hosted runners.
Diego Morales: LGTM after bumping setup-node to v4; confirm Node 20 passes all integration tests in the matrix.
Evelyn Chen: Ran a full matrix in a temporary branch; all tests passed in the Node 20 matrix. CI run id: 39871234 (see checks).
Marta Ruiz: Approving — this will reduce a lot of noise. Minor nit: call out GH Action version pins in docs for future auditing.
Evelyn Chen: Added tools/gh-actions/upgrade.md with pinned versions and rollforward instructions.
release_notes: Refactor CI pipelines: split monolithic workflow into lint/test/release, bump GitHub Actions to latest majors, upgrade default Node runtime to 20 where supported, add cache warmup and TTL pruning to reduce flakiness and speed up PR validation.
notes_for_ops: Rollout plan: enable workflows on ci-rollout branches for 48h, monitor pipeline duration and cache hit rate. If CI time increases >10% or cache hit rate drops >5% revert branch or toggle to previous main workflow. Contact: @evelyn. Automated revert documented in README_CI.md.
backout_instructions: To revert: gh pr checkout <revert-pr> or revert the merge commit and re-run release workflows. Follow docs in tools/gh-actions/upgrade.md for action version pins.
